sentences.text:
Also heard on I.A. No.13260/2025, which is an application filed under Section 430(1) of Bnss,
2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant no.1 to appellant no.6.
The appellants have been tried and convicted by order dated 16.05.2025 passed by 18th Additional Session Court, Bhopal in S.T No. 555/2019.

The appellants namely Vikas, Praveen, Nagendra,
Ramesh and Satyendra have been tried and convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 419 read with section 120B, 420 read with section 120B, 467 read with section 120B, 468 read with section 120B, 471 read with section 120B of IPC and sentenced to suffer R.I for 3 years and with fine and further under section 3(d) (2) read with section 4 of the M.P Recognized Examination Act, and sentenced to suffer R.I for 3 years and with fine respectively with default stipulations.

The appellant namely Shivkaran have been tried and convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 419 read with section 120B, 420 read with section 120B, 467 read with section 120B, 468 read with section 120B, 471 read with section 120B of IPC and sentenced to suffer R.I for 3 years and with fine and 2 CRA-5308-2025 further under section 3(d)(1) (2) read with section 4 of the M.P Recognized Examination Act, and sentenced to suffer R.I for 3 years and with fine respectively with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellants submit that vide order dated 02.06.2025 passed by this Court,
the suspension of sentence as granted by the trial court was extended till the next date of hearing.

As per period of incarceration during the trial, the appellants have already undergone substantial Vikas Singh vs Cbi Vyapam on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150190238/
1 period of sentence, which is almost 1/4 of their jail sentence.
The maximum sentence imposed is only of three years.
This appeal is not going to be heard finally in near future.
During the trial, the appellants have never misused the liberty of bail.
Therefore, the prayer is made to suspend the jail sentence of the appellants.
Learned counsel for the respondent has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the appeal, the I.A. No.13260/2025 is allowed.
It is directed that the bail granted by the trial court shall continue on the same terms and conditions imposed by the court below during the pendency of this appeal.
List this appeal for final hearing in due course.
